change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: A backup code alone logs in, because a dummy totpCode skips the password check
findings.body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new branch at line 131 runs when `credentials.backupCode` is set. A request with `{email, backupCode, totpCode: "x"}` skips the password check and then passes on the backup code alone. The TOTP path already had this shape, but there the second factor rotates. Backup codes are static 40-bit secrets, and the user is told to download them to a text file, so a leaked file plus the email is now a full login. The login UI clears `totpCode` when switching to backup mode, so only direct callers of the credentials endpoint can do this. Verify the password whenever `user.password` exists, regardless of `totpCode`. Or at least skip the password check only when no `backupCode` is present.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code list is read in `findUnique` at line 73, then rewritten whole at lines 149-156. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either update lands, so a "single use" code is accepted twice. Two concurrent logins with different codes can overwrite each other's `null`, which makes the used code valid again. Consider a conditional update, for example `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read, and treat a count of 0 as an incorrect code. The same applies to disable.ts, though that endpoint deletes all codes afterwards.

findings.title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step by Escape or an outside click leaves the UI wrong and the codes lost
findings.body: 2FA is already enabled on the server once `enable` returns 200 (line 135). The caller's `onOpenChange` in apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 only toggles `enableModalOpen`. It does not call `onEnable`, so `viewer.me` is not invalidated and the switch still shows disabled. The `step` state is also not reset, so reopening the dialog shows the codes screen again. The Cancel button is hidden on this step (lines 222-231), but the dialog's close mechanisms are still active. Backup codes are never shown again by anything else. Make the dialog's close path on this step behave like the Close button (`resetState(); onEnable()`), or block dismissal on this step.

findings.title: "Please generate them in your settings" points to a feature that does not exist
findings.body: The only place codes are generated is `setup.ts`, during the enable flow, and nothing lets a user regenerate them. The message is shown when a user whose `backupCodes` is null picks "Lost access" (login.tsx:158 and DisableTwoFactorModal). That is every user who enabled 2FA before this migration. Those users get a message telling them to do something they cannot do, and they are locked out if they lose the authenticator. Either add a regenerate action or change the message and plan a path for existing users.

findings.title: A non-string backupCode in the request body causes an unhandled 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` throws a TypeError if the JSON body has a number or object. The handler also `throw`s at line 51, unlike the explicit 400 responses used elsewhere in this handler. Validate `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` and return a 400 with an error code. The same applies to `credentials.backupCode` at next-auth-options.ts:144, which is less exposed because it is stringified through the form post.

findings.title: Component is named TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export of `BackupCode.tsx` is `TwoFactor`, the same name as the TOTP component in TwoFactor.tsx. This is confusing in stack traces and devtools. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

findings.title: The new login and disable-with-backup-code paths have no test
findings.body: The e2e only exercises the download, copy and close buttons. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, that a used code is rejected the second time, or that disabling with a backup code works. The TODO at line 12 admits this. These are the security-critical branches of this change (next-auth-options.ts:131-156 and disable.ts:48-67). Line 50 adds a FIXME saying an existing assertion passes vacuously; that assertion is not fixed here.

findings.title: Copy shows a success toast without awaiting the clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` returns a promise that rejects when permission is denied or the context is insecure. The rejection is unhandled and the "Backup codes copied!" toast is shown regardless. Since these codes cannot be shown again, the user could believe they saved them when they did not. Await the call and show the toast only on success.

contracts.action: Login with backup code (new credentials field, consumes a code)
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing TOTP branch at next-auth-options.ts:157-187 in the same authorize function
contracts.before_after: The TOTP branch only reads state. The new branch deletes the used code by rewriting the encrypted list, but does it by read-modify-write. The password check at line 121 still keys on `totpCode`, not on the second-factor type.
contracts.visible_effect: login.tsx:156-158 maps IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes to messages. Success pushes the callbackUrl.
contracts.failure_mode: A concurrent reuse of the same code is accepted. A dummy totpCode skips password verification. A user with null backupCodes sees a message pointing to a nonexistent settings action.

contracts.action: Enable 2FA now ends on a backup-codes screen; onEnable is called only from the Close button
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `onEnable()` was called directly on enable success (old line 134), which closed the dialog and invalidated `viewer.me`
contracts.before_after: Before, success closed the dialog and refreshed the switch. Now success moves to the backup-codes step, and the refresh happens only if the user clicks Close (line 269). The parent's onOpenChange only toggles open state.
contracts.visible_effect: Dismissing by Escape or an outside click leaves the switch showing disabled although 2FA is on, and reopening shows the codes step again.
contracts.failure_mode: Codes are lost, because setup.ts returns them only once. The UI state is stale until a reload.

contracts.equivalent_path: The TOTP check at disable.ts:69-100 in the same handler
contracts.before_after: The password check at lines 40-45 runs before both branches. Both branches end in the same update, which now also nulls backupCodes (line 107). The backup branch does not consume the code, which is fine because all codes are cleared.
contracts.visible_effect: The modal shows the matching error from DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:67-78 and calls onDisable on 200.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-string body value gives a 500. The handler has no rate limit on repeated guesses, as before for TOTP.

summary: The backup-code feature is mostly coherent, but two defects need fixing. First, `authorize` skips the password check whenever `totpCode` is non-empty, so email, a backup code and a dummy `totpCode` log in with no password. Second, dismissing the enable dialog on the backup-codes step by Escape or an outside click never calls `onEnable`, so the switch stays stale and the one-time codes are lost. Smaller points: code consumption is not atomic, the \"generate them in your settings\" message points to a feature that does not exist, a non-string `backupCode` causes a 500 in disable.ts, and nothing tests the login or disable backup-code paths.
